answer: A stake-bond registry resists Sybil attacks by making each identity expensive: to join, an agent must lock a refundable bond in a public cipher-secured escrow. One honest agent pays once, but an attacker spawning a gale of fake identities must fund every one, so cost scales with the number of sock puppets. If an identity is caught cheating, its bond is slashed and the loss is announced as a quiet whisper across the reputation ledger, so the same funds cannot be recycled. The bond returns only after a clean record, turning identity creation from free into a priced, auditable act.
